data.name: Alayna
data.gender_notes: Alayna is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'alayna', meaning 'on us', which symbolizes the idea of being bestowed upon, or chosen by Allah. In a feminine context, Alayna can be interpreted as 'heavenly one', or 'exalted'. The name Alayna carries the meaning “Heavenly one, exalted” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Alayna usually hope their child will grow to embody heavenly one, exalted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Alayna is also associated with the story of Aisha bint Abu Bakr (RA), who was known for her deep faith and dedication to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
data.etymology: Alayna belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Heavenly one, exalted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alayna total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_urdu.name: عالینا

in_hindi.name: अलायना

in_pashto.name: عالينا

in_english.name: Alayna
in_english.long_meaning: The name Alayna is derived from the Arabic root 'ع ل و' (al-ʿalaw), which means 'to rise,' 'to elevate,' or 'exalted.' This name symbolizes high status, spiritual ascension, and moral excellence. While not directly mentioned in the Quran, the root 'ع ل و' appears in various verses, emphasizing elevation and exaltation by Allah. In Islamic tradition, names like Alayna are chosen to inspire virtues such as humility, piety, and a quest for spiritual growth. The name Alayna is used across different Muslim cultures, reflecting a shared aspiration for moral and spiritual elevation.
